text: Three deadlines this week, Mum in hospital, the boiler broke and the kids have half term. I don't know where to start.
Too much. Everything at once. Sat on the bathroom floor for ten minutes just to breathe.
Wedding planning is eating my life. Florist, caterer, seating plan, Aunt Lola's demands.
Inbox has 412 unread. I closed it and stared at the wall.
First week as a manager. Everyone needs something from me every minute. I've forgotten to eat lunch three days running.
Moving house, starting a new job and Pedro's family visiting. All this week.
I can't keep all the plates spinning. Something's going to drop and I don't know which one.
New baby, toddler with chickenpox, partner away for work. I'm drowning.
The to-do list is longer than the day. I just keep adding to it.
Exams, part-time job, and Kaveh needing me every night since his breakup. I'm stretched thin.
Sensory overload at the shopping centre. Lights, music, crowds. Had to leave the trolley and go sit in the car.
All the paperwork after Dad's death. Bank, pension, council, solicitor. Each one wants a different form.
Overwhelmed by kindness today, honestly. Fifty messages after the news. I can't answer them all.
Renovation chaos. Dust everywhere, no kitchen, the builder hasn't turned up and the budget's gone.
So many decisions about Mum's care. Every option has a cost. I keep making spreadsheets and crying.
Christmas prep: gifts for 23 people, hosting, a work party, the school play. And it's only the 2nd.
Had a panic in the supermarket because there were too many types of bread. It's not about the bread.
New country, new language, new job. Everything takes ten times the effort. My brain is full.
Swamped at work. Three people quit and their work landed on me.
I'm juggling caring for Grandpa, the kids and a full-time job. Some days I just stand in the kitchen not knowing what to do first.
Thesis due in a month, data analysis not done, supervisor on leave. Spiralling.
The news today was too much. Turned it off and sat in silence.
Everything is urgent and nothing is getting done. Lingering dread about Monday.
Twins plus a puppy was a mistake. A lovely mistake. But a mistake.
Too many people needing me this week. Selin, the team, the kids, my mother. I'm empty.
Starting uni is a lot. Lectures, timetables, finding rooms, meeting people. My head is spinning.
Flooded basement, insurance calls, neighbours asking for help with theirs. Haven't slept.
Big launch day. Twenty bugs reported in the first hour. Slack is on fire.
Grief and paperwork and work emails all at once. I can't hold it all.
Bit overwhelmed by the open-plan office. Noise everywhere. Headphones on all day.
Running the shop alone while Kenzo's in hospital. Deliveries, customers, accounts. I'm barely keeping my head above water.
The doctor gave me so much information about the diagnosis I couldn't take any of it in.
Hosting fourteen people for Eid. Kitchen is chaos. Nani is 'helping' by criticising.
Can't think straight. Too many tabs open in my brain.
Working two jobs, studying at night, sending money home. Something has to give.
So many emotions at the wedding. Joy, nerves, missing Dad. I was a mess all day in the best and worst ways.
Got handed the whole project after Lucas left. Two weeks to deliver what he had three months for.
Kids screaming, phone ringing, dinner burning, doorbell. All at once. I just stood there.
The divorce paperwork is endless. Every page is a decision about the rest of my life.
I said yes to too many things this month. Calendar is solid colour. No white space anywhere.
Nursing shift from hell. Two emergencies, one death, a new admission and no breaks.
Too much input today. Need dark, quiet, nothing.
Packing up the house to sell. Thirty years of stuff. Every drawer is a memory and a decision.
Group project, solo project, part-time job, Mira's birthday. I keep writing lists and losing them.
Everything feels like too much lately. Even small things like replying to messages.
Third funeral this year. Can't process one before the next.
Audit at work, sick kid at home, car in the garage. My brain feels like static.
The new software, the new process, the new manager. Too much change in one month.
Volunteering, coaching, the PTA, work. I'm the person who can't say no and it's catching up with me.
Opened the letter from the hospital and read three paragraphs of words I didn't understand. Had to put it down.
House full of relatives for the week. Lovely but I haven't had a minute to myself.
I'm behind on everything. Bills, emails, laundry, life admin. It's a mountain.
Teaching five classes, marking, parents' evening, inspection next week. Running on adrenaline and coffee.
Feeling buried. Work, family, the move, Ilya's surgery. One more thing and I'll crack.
The festival was amazing but so loud and crowded. I needed to leave halfway.
Starting my own business means I'm the accountant, the designer, the salesperson and the cleaner. Exhausting and too much.
Overwhelmed. Just that word today.
Mum's dementia diagnosis, my sister abroad, Dad not coping. It's all on me now.
Election, war, climate. My feed is too much. Deleted the app for a week.
Picking up three shifts plus the course plus helping Delia with the baby. My head is full of noise.
Tax return, visa renewal and lease renewal all due the same week. Who designed this.
I tried to plan the week and gave up halfway through. Too many moving parts.
First week back after maternity leave. Pumping in the cupboard, 200 emails, sobbing in the car park at lunch.
Everything hit at once today and I cried at my desk. Lukas brought me a tea and didn't say anything.
Too many choices for the new flat. Every listing looks the same now. I can't decide anything.
I keep forgetting things. Appointments, birthdays, why I walked into the room. Too much in my head.
Big family gathering, everyone talking at once, kids running everywhere. Loved it, needed a lie-down after.
The week from hell: car crash (minor, everyone's fine), work crisis, Babajide's hospital visit.
Not a bad day, just too full. Back-to-back from 7am to 10pm.
Wanted to help everyone and ended up helping no one well. Spread too thin.
